We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) from commercially available chemicals, total price <= $405. We need to propose route JSON.

We have target SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This looks like a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 1-...?). The template 222683 seems to convert a methyl ester (COC(=O)OCH3) attached to a carbonyl? Actually retro_smarts: [CH3]-O- C(=O)-O-? Wait: The template is for ester cleavage? The retro_smarts: [CH3;D1;+0:1]-[O;H0;D2;+0:4]-[C:3]=[O;D1;H0:2]>>C-O-C(=O)-O-C(=O)-O-[CH3;D1;+0:1].[O;D1;H0:2]=[C:3]-[OH;D1;+0:4]. This is a retro-esterification? It splits methyl ester into methyl alcohol and acid? Actually product is the target (ester). Reactants are methyl alcohol (CH3O) and acid (C=O OH). So applying this template forward (i.e., retrosynthesis) would give precursors: methanol and the corresponding carboxylic acid (the acid part). So we can propose a single-step retrosynthesis: target = methyl ester of a carboxylic acid. Precursors: methanol (CH3OH) and the corresponding acid: the bicyclic ketone with carboxylic acid (instead of methyl ester). Let's generate acid SMILES: replace COC(=O) with COOH? The target: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. That's methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone acid. The acid SMILES would be O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O? Actually the carbonyl carbon attached to OCH3 is the carbonyl of the ester. So acid would be O=C(O)[C@]12... So acid SMILES: O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O. Let's verify: The target has COC( ... )=O meaning OCH3 attached to carbonyl carbon. So acid is same but with OH instead of OCH3. So acid SMILES: O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O.

Now we need to check if this template applies to target. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id 222683.
